Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

Head of Electronics & Software

Purpose

We are looking for a Head of Electronics & Software to lead and develop the engineering capability behind some of the most critical systems in our spacecraft.

This is a senior leadership role combining people leadership, engineering excellence, organisational development and technical breadth . You will lead a multidisciplinary organisation spanning:

Avionics, communications and electrical power systems

Flight software (FSW)

Guidance, navigation and control (GNC)

Electrical wiring and interconnection systems (EWIS), including harness engineering

Future projects and advanced electronics and software development

You will be responsible for ensuring our teams have the people, skills, processes, tools and engineering standards needed to deliver ambitious space programmes today, while building the capabilities we will need for the future.

This is not a role for someone looking to step away from engineering. We are looking for a leader who can engage credibly with highly technical teams, challenge constructively, develop strong technical leaders and help create an environment where exceptional engineering can happen.

Matrix Organisation

Our engineering teams work in a matrix organisation, combining strong functional leadership with project-based delivery.

As Head of Electronics & Software, you will lead the functional organisation, developing its people and capabilities while working closely with Project Managers, Project Chief Engineers, technical authorities and engineering Leads responsible for programme delivery.

You will:

Lead and develop Project Leads, discipline Leads, Principal Engineers and transversal engineering resources

Partner with project leadership to align capability, resources and priorities with programme needs

Help teams navigate competing priorities across projects

Ensure clear ownership and accountability between functional leadership and project execution

Build an organisation capable of supporting multiple programmes as the company grows

Success in this environment requires collaboration, influence and sound engineering judgement rather than centralising every technical decision.

Role Boundaries

This role owns the strength and effectiveness of the Electronics & Software organisation : its people, capability, engineering practices, tools, standards and functional budget.

You will create the environment in which our technical teams can perform at their best, providing mentoring, challenge and access to expertise while supporting technical and project leadership in making strong engineering decisions.

Project technical decisions and product technical authority remain within the relevant project and technical organisations. Your role is to ensure they are supported by a highly capable engineering organisation with the right expertise, methods and resources.

Key Responsibilities

People, Hiring & Organisation

You will build and shape a high-performing Electronics & Software organisation.

Your responsibilities will include:

Owning workforce and headcount planning across the function

Recruiting and retaining exceptional engineering talent

Developing clear job families, role levels and assessment standards

Partnering with Talent Acquisition, engineering Leads and hiring managers to maintain a high technical hiring bar

Leading promotion, compensation and organisational planning within the function

Building succession plans and reducing key-person dependencies in specialist areas

Creating an organisation that remains lean, scalable and aligned with current and future programme needs

Line Management & Development

Developing strong engineers and technical leaders will be a major part of the role.

You will:

Lead and develop the managers, Leads and senior engineers within your organisation

Establish meaningful objectives aligned with project and company priorities

Build clear development and technical career paths

Strengthen mentoring, coaching and leadership capability across the organisation

Create opportunities for engineers to gain experience across design, integration, test and operations

Address performance challenges fairly and constructively

Build a culture where progression is based on demonstrated capability, impact and organisational need

Engineering Processes, Standards & Compliance

You will help define how excellent electronics and software engineering is done across the company .

This includes:

Owning and continuously improving engineering practices across electronics, software, GNC and electrical/harness engineering

Establishing practical standards for electronics design, software development, testing, modelling, reviews and verification

Ensuring teams understand and can effectively apply the relevant processes

Supporting certification readiness, audits and continuous improvement, including applicable EN9100 requirements

Working closely with Quality, Safety, Systems Engineering and the Chief Engineer organisation

Using lessons from development, testing and operations to continuously improve engineering practices

Our aim is not process for process's sake. We want processes that are lean, pragmatic and proportionate to engineering risk .

Engineering Tools & Ways of Working

You will ensure our engineers have the tools and engineering environment needed to work effectively and at scale.

This includes capability across:

Electronics and PCB design

Harness CAD

Software development, build and configuration toolchains

Automated testing

GNC analysis and modelling

Software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop environments

Simulation and shared test infrastructure

You will drive standardisation, adoption and good engineering practice while partnering with Digital, IT, Procurement, Quality and other engineering teams.

The goal is simple: engineering work should be efficient, traceable, reproducible and ready to scale. 

Project Support & Resource Planning

You will work closely with our projects to ensure they have access to the Electronics & Software capability they need.

You will:

Mentor engineering Leads and provide senior technical guidance where needed

Support major technical and engineering reviews

Maintain visibility of capability gaps, resource constraints and significant engineering risks

Work with project leadership to resolve resource requirements through hiring, development, internal mobility or external support

Anticipate future capacity constraints before they become programme blockers

Help resolve cross-project resource and organisational conflicts

Contribute to the company-wide electronics and software strategy alongside the Chief of Engineering and CTO

Shape future capabilities, reusable technologies, R&D priorities and obsolescence strategies

Budget

You will own the Electronics & Software functional budget and forecast, including:

Headcount and personnel planning

Engineering tools and licences

Relevant shared simulation and test capability

Training and development

Functional team travel

You will work closely with Finance, Procurement, Digital and project leadership to ensure investment supports both immediate programme needs and longer-term engineering capability.

Requirements

We are looking for someone who combines credible engineering depth with proven organisational leadership .

You should bring:

Strong hands-on engineering experience in at least one of the following: avionics, electronics, embedded systems, flight software, GNC or electrical systems

Enough technical breadth to operate effectively across several of these disciplines and understand how they interact

Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams in a complex product environment

Proven formal line-management experience, including developing managers and technical leaders

Experience hiring, developing and building engineering organisations

Experience with organisational design, workforce and capacity planning

Experience creating or improving engineering processes, tools, standards and ways of working

Experience operating within a matrix organisation and supporting multiple projects or programmes

Strong coaching, mentoring, communication and influencing skills

The technical credibility to challenge senior engineers while empowering the appropriate technical owners to make decisions

A pragmatic approach to engineering quality, assurance and compliance, including relevant EN9100 practices

Experience in spacecraft, launch vehicles, aerospace, defence, aviation, robotics or another complex safety-critical engineering environment would be particularly relevant.

We are looking for a leader who: 

Leads with high standards, humility and low ego

Enjoys developing people rather than simply directing them

Empowers strong technical Leads and avoids becoming a bottleneck

Can challenge experienced engineers constructively

Makes decisions using data and sound engineering judgement

Balances immediate programme pressures with long-term organisational capability

Creates clarity where responsibilities cross organisational boundaries

Promotes transparency, accountability, collaboration and continuous learning

Believes in extreme ownership and engineering first principles 

Remains close enough to the engineering to understand the challenges our teams are solving

Location & Travel

This is a leadership role with teams and stakeholders across our European organisation, so regular face-to-face engagement is important.

You should expect to spend time across our main European sites, with additional travel where required for team leadership, recruitment, major engineering reviews, audits and project support.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

We are seeking an experienced and motivated EMC/EMI Engineer to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing design recommendations and establishing test policies related to Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) for our spacecraft applications. This role requires a thorough understanding of EMC/EMI principles, spacecraft systems, and industry standards to ensure the reliability and functionality of our spacecraft in harsh space environments.

Key Responsibilities: 

Design and Development: 

Provide expert guidance on EMC/EMI design practices to ensure spacecraft systems meet all relevant standards and requirements.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate EMC/EMI considerations into the design phase of spacecraft systems and subsystems.

Review and analyze design documents, schematics, and layout plans to identify potential EMC/EMI issues.

Testing and Validation: 

Develop and implement comprehensive EMC/EMI test plans and procedures for spacecraft systems.

Conduct EMC/EMI testing, including pre-compliance and compliance testing.

Analyze test data, identify non-conformities, and recommend corrective actions to resolve EMC/EMI issues.

Standards and technological watch: 

Ensure all designs and test procedures comply with relevant EMC/EMI standards

Stay updated with the latest developments in EMC/EMI standards and incorporate them into design and testing processes.

Documentation and Reporting: 

Prepare detailed technical reports, test summaries, and design documentation related to EMC/EMI activities.

Maintain accurate records of all test results, design recommendations, and corrective actions.

Collaboration and Support: 

Work closely with system engineers, hardware designers, and other stakeholders to address EMC/EMI challenges throughout the product development lifecycle.

Provide technical support and training to engineering teams on EMC/EMI best practices and mitigation techniques.

Qualifications: 

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related field.

Minimum of 5 years of experience in EMC/EMI engineering, preferably in the aerospace or defense industry.

Strong knowledge of EMC/EMI principles, test methods, and mitigation techniques.

Experience with EMC/EMI standards, such as MIL-STD-461, CISPR, and DO-160.

Proficiency in using EMC/EMI testing equipment, including spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, and EMI receivers.

Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.

Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications: 

Experience with spacecraft systems and subsystems.

Knowledge of signal integrity and power integrity as they relate to EMC/EMI.

Experience with simulation tools for EMC/EMI analysis.

We want you as a talented AIT MGSE Engineer to help us in our mission by designing and delivering the MGSEs needed for the preparation of our next capsule.

Key Responsibilities 

In your capacity as MAIT MGSE Engineer, your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day duties will include:

Work closely with Engineering and AIT colleagues to understand and refine the requirements/timelines for the different MGSEs that we will need for various assembly or testing activities.

Conceptualise, design (CAD including manufacturing drawings), procure and commission the MGSEs.

Confirm with mechanical analysis/hand calculations/proof tests that the design is compatible with the external loads.

Discuss with suppliers the MGSE designs for ease of manufacturing and with the most adequate processes.

Follow up the manufacturing/procurement with the suppliers (with the support of our supply chain team) and answer any technical questions/concerns ensuring timely delivery of all items.

Provide necessary instructions and support the assembly/commissioning/ implementation of these MGSEs.

What we would love to see from you 

In the role of MAIT MGSE Engineer ideally, you will have the following:

Mechanical / Aerospace engineering degree or similar with focus on machine / structural design.

Minimum 2 years of experience in CAD design + drafting (using Siemens NX or similar) and FE analysis (using Hypermesh or similar).

Good understanding of machine design and different manufacturing processes (e.g. machining, welding, etc), design for manufacturing and GD&T.

Familiarity with standard margin calculation methodologies for various applications like beams, bolted joints, welds, etc.

Experience with design of test setups/jigs/fixtures and planning/execution of mechanical tests in-house would be a plus.

Good at documentation including design descriptions, assembly instructions, test reports, etc.

Creative with innovative ideas and technical problem solving/troubleshooting skills.

Basic hands-on experience with mechanical assembly and simple machining tools like drilling machine.

Previous experience in space AIT and MGSE design would be highly appreciated.

Good English communication skills (German would be a plus).

Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

We are developing, producing and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable orbital vehicle designed to carry cargo and, in the longer term, potentially crew.

To support the ramp-up of our production activities in Munich, we are looking for a Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) Technician - Level 2 with strong practical experience in radiographic testing (RT/X-ray) and penetrant testing (PT). Ultrasonic testing (UT) experience is an advantage.

You will perform and document inspections on critical space components and assemblies. In your day-to-day work, you will collaborate with Production, Quality and Engineering teams, as well as external providers and the appointed Responsible Level 3. Your rigor will directly contribute to the conformity, traceability and reliability of flight hardware.

Your mission

You will prepare and perform NDT inspections in accordance with approved procedures and acceptance criteria, assess results within the scope of your qualification, and alert the relevant stakeholders when you identify a discrepancy or technical concern.

What you will do

Perform radiographic testing (RT/X-ray) and penetrant testing (PT) on production parts, welds, structures and other hardware in accordance with applicable procedures.

Prepare parts, verify inspection conditions, and use the required equipment and consumables.

Interpret and evaluate indications within the scope of your qualification and against approved acceptance criteria; seek guidance or escalate complex or ambiguous cases.

Produce complete inspection reports and maintain traceability of results, equipment, parameters and applicable documents.

Check the condition and validity of inspection equipment, and report any need for maintenance, verification or replacement.

Coordinate with Production to schedule inspections at the right stage and help resolve inspection-related production blockers.

Raise non-conformities and contribute to root-cause investigations, corrective actions and their follow-up.

Contribute to updating work instructions, procedures, inspection plans and report templates, under the coordination of authorized personnel.

When needed, coordinate inspections performed by external providers and check that their deliverables and supporting documentation are complete.

Contribute to the continuous improvement of NDT practices and the development of internal capabilities, including UT where your experience allows.

Follow the site’s safety, quality and document-control requirements.

What you bring

Level 2 qualification in radiographic testing (RT/X-ray) and penetrant testing (PT) under EN 4179, NAS 410, ISO 9712; current qualifications are strongly preferred.

Professional experience in the space industry is required, ideally involving flight hardware or critical equipment.

Practical experience inspecting welds, metallic structures, pressure vessels, propulsion systems, machined parts or composite components.

Ability to read drawings, specifications, procedures and acceptance criteria, and produce accurate, clear inspection reports.

Good understanding of inspection traceability, equipment control and the handling of non-conforming results.

Ability to work within the scope of your qualification and consult the Level 3 or technical focal points whenever a decision falls outside that scope.

Professional working proficiency in English, both spoken and written, to operate in an international environment.

Especially valuable

UT qualification or practical experience, particularly inspecting critical parts or structures.

Experience with digital radiography, phased-array UT, automated inspection or composite inspection.

Experience working with a Responsible Level 3, external NDT providers or certification bodies.

Experience preparing or reviewing procedures, technical instructions or inspection plans.

How you work

Rigorous and detail-oriented, with a consistent focus on conformity and traceability.

Sound technical judgment and a pragmatic, production-focused mindset.

Autonomous and organized, with clear communication whenever a discrepancy or concern arises.

Comfortable collaborating with Production, Quality, Engineering and external providers.

Motivated to help build robust NDT capabilities for demanding space hardware.

About Seamflow 

Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.

Where we are:

Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

$4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team 

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role 

A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them.

You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for 

We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not.

What we're actually screening for:

You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better.

You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters.

You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is.

You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful.

You go to the source. You'll watch a technical reviewer work through a real file, and you'll design for what they actually do rather than what the process diagram says.

Signals we like, none of them required:

design engineering or front-end roles at somewhere like Linear, Vercel, Notion or Figma, a design system you built and maintained, work on interfaces where people review or correct AI output, founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup.

This is probably not for you if 

You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get 

Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

About the role: What's in the Box

The Logistics Tribe builds the systems powering end-to-end delivery across North America, Europe and Australia/New Zealand: getting fresh ingredients into our facilities, giving customers the best delivery options the network can support, and tracking every box to the customer's door. Today it is a single engineering team - two staff engineers, a data engineer and seven mid-to-senior engineers - led by the Director of Engineering, owning that software and keeping it running in production. You will join as an Engineering Manager and take line management of the seven.

The work is operations-heavy and business-critical, spread across different subdomains. You won't own a fixed backlog in one corner of the domain; the team's scope follows where the business pressure is. That is reflected in how we work: rather than one fixed squad, the team organises into small, project-focused pods that form and dissolve as projects start and finish. In a typical sprint, your engineers might be spread across three projects with three different product managers.

Strategy and technical direction are things we shape together - staff engineers, product managers and you all contributing, nobody working from a script handed down. You own the people and the delivery of your engineers.

The role reports to the Director of Engineering for Logistics Tech; your team is spread across two geographies.

What you'll do: The Recipe

  • Lead and grow a team of mid-to-senior engineers: set clear expectations, give regular and honest feedback, and own their development - including building the case when someone is ready for the next level.
  • Own the people and stay technical. This role carries real hands-on expectations - you still deliver code yourself, not management at a distance.
  • Keep raising the team's AI bar: role-model it in your own work, and push the workflows where AI genuinely changes how fast we deliver.
  • Make our project-based way of working work for people. You lead project staffing with the Director of Engineering and the product managers, putting engineers where the work and their growth both fit. You limit how many projects anyone carries, and you keep handovers clean so nobody becomes a single point of failure.
  • Own the delivery health of your team's work together with the product managers and the engineers leading each project: realistic plans, sound quality, and systems that stay reliable once shipped.
  • Hire and onboard well - you'll be building the team's balance of skills as projects and domains shift under you.
  • Champion the engineering practices we care about: behaviour-driven tests for every business use case, and small iterations.
  • Help shape tribe culture as part of the leadership team, in a setup that is deliberately flat and collaborative.

What you'll bring: The Ingredients

  • At least 2 years leading mid-to-senior engineers in an agile environment, backed by 6+ years of total engineering experience - you've run development and growth conversations and seen people through to promotion.
  • Comfort leading people through changing project boundaries - this is a team that reforms around projects, not one that sits still.
  • A backend-leaning technical grounding - event-driven microservices, Kubernetes, Kafka, relational databases, CI/CD - with real BDD/TDD habits that make large refactorings safe. You don't need to be the deepest engineer in the room, but you need to earn the team's respect.
  • Daily, practical experience building with AI tooling: you've shipped real work with it, you know where it fails, and you learn as readily from others as they learn from you.
  • A product-oriented mindset: you can reason about the business problem, prioritise for customer impact, and push back on low-value scope.
  • Genuine interest in physical-world and supply-chain problems. You want to understand how the operation actually works; logistics or carrier integration experience is a plus.

Above all, we are looking for individuals who will make HelloFresh better. We believe there are many different ways of developing skills and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don't "tick all the boxes" but think you'd thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.
